title: Evaluation of Potential Partner Characteristics by Warias in Indonesia
content: Little is known about the partner preferences of waria, male-to-female transgender people, in Indonesia. This study differs from previous research by focusing on characteristics that warias find unacceptable in a partner rather than on the desirable characteristics. In addition, a special feature was the impact of two physical indicators of poor oral health -bad breath (halitosis) and crooked teeth- on the attractiveness of potential mates. These factors were assessed along with indicators of the most common negative determinants of partner attractiveness, i.e., physical unattractiveness and perceived low status. In addition, it was examined how these factors related to personal characteristics, including self-perceived attractiveness, the importance of physical attractiveness, subjective social status, and intrasexual competition (competition with same-sex individuals for potential partners). The findings showed that indicators of a poor oral health, i.e., a bad breath and particularly ugly teeth were important factors that made warias reject a partner, more so than an unattractive face, another background, being overweight, being poor, or having a low education. Ugly teeth were even, after laziness, a bad body odor and a bad figure, the most important factor to reject a potential or actual partner. The rejection of such characteristics was especially strong among those who found themselves physically attractive, and attached much value to physical attractiveness.
